name: Contestability Is Institutional Not Individual
text: Kissinger's objection is that systems reaching conclusions humans cannot trace undermine the Enlightenment premise of knowledge acquired by reasoning individuals. Kaal's position is that the Enlightenment rested on institutions that let claims be contested, verified and credited by those competent to do so, rather than on individual traceability. The protected claim supplies one such institutional step: at stage three of the pipeline, reputation-weighted validation adjudicates semantic faithfulness and consistency and records the result on the WDAG, in place of a decidable decision procedure. Whether an institutional verification step of that kind also answers the traceability objection is the essay's argument and not a result of the claim.
scope_conditions: The position accepts that opaque, centralized and unaccountable intelligence does end the Enlightenment. It disputes only the claim that this is the single available path.
The protected claim establishes the replacement of a decidable decision procedure at one pipeline stage. It does not establish that individual traceability of an inference can be dispensed with.
The position is an argument about institutional design. No reputation-weighted verification layer operating at this scale has been built or tested.
